subject: Discovery recap: data handling, retention, and audit logs (Acme Health)
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Taylor Morgan <taylor.morgan@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: data handling, retention, and audit logs (Acme Health)

Hi Taylor —

Thanks again for the time today. Wanted to capture the key points from our discovery call so we have a clear set of success criteria and follow-ups. Please correct anything I missed.

Quick summary of what we heard
- Primary pain: unpredictable token-level cost and lack of a repeatable, auditable data-handling workflow for PHI/PII that meets your compliance team’s constraints.
- Current stack: custom REST API -> in-house preprocessor -> logs to S3 (unencrypted objects currently), Auth via Okta, some requests routed to legacy LLM proxy.
- Immediate goal: run a 6-week pilot of Redwood with field-level redaction and strict logging controls, then evaluate for wider rollout.

Success criteria (customer-stated)
1) No raw PII stored in logs (SSNs, full MRNs, payment card numbers).
2) Field-level redaction or deterministic hashing before any persistent storage.
3) Configurable retention windows (short-term request logs removable within 30 days; audit trails preserved per compliance needs).
4) Strong auditability: immutable audit events, exportable logs for third-party auditors.
5) Performance: equivalent latency to current proxy at 95th percentile for typical clinical workloads.

Specific data/privacy constraints we discussed
- PII handling: prefer redaction or irreversible hashing before write; any intermediate copies must be encrypted and access-restricted.
- Retention: clinical request logs should be retained no longer than 30 days by default; audit logs may need longer retention (customer indicated up to 7 years for compliance records) but must have PII removed or pseudonymized.
- Audit logs: require tamper-evident entries (append-only), export in NDJSON/CSV for auditors, with RBAC for access.
- Redaction requirements: support both regex-based configurable redaction and plugin-based field mapping (so they can declare a field as PHI). Need deterministic pseudonymization for identity mapping in analytics.

Attachments I shared: redwood_privacy_brief.pdf (high-level controls), MA_Template_v1.docx (sample mutual action plan).

Open questions for your team
- Can you confirm which fields you consider PHI (list example top 10 fields)?
- Is 30-day retention for request logs a hard requirement or a target?
- Do you require on-prem key management (HSM/KMS) or is cloud-managed KMS acceptable?

Proposed next steps
1) Technical deep-dive with our RSEs to validate field-level redaction architecture (propose Tue 2026-02-24, 10am PT).
2) We’ll share an initial SOC2 summary & our privacy brief (attached).
3) We’ll produce a scoped pilot proposal and ballpark pricing for a 6-month pilot.
4) Please send back your security questionnaire (you mentioned you’d attach it) and a list of PHI fields.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if you want to walk through this.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
diego.fernandez@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0184

Attachments: redwood_privacy_brief.pdf (PDF), MA_Template_v1.docx (DOCX)

From: Taylor Morgan <taylor.morgan@acmehealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: data handling, retention, and audit logs (Acme Health)

Diego —

Thanks for the clear recap. This captures the conversation well. A couple clarifications/additions from our side:

- PHI scope: at minimum we need SSN, full MRN, date of birth, full name, payment card numbers to be redacted or pseudonymized prior to any long-term storage. We will send a canonical list of fields by EOD tomorrow.
- Retention: 30 days for raw request/response payloads is a requirement for our privacy policy. Audit logs (events about decisioning and access) need to be retained for up to 7 years but must be stored in a way that PII is not directly reconstructable. Deterministic hashing for identifiers is acceptable if it’s irreversible by us.
- KMS: we prefer customer-managed keys (HSM) for encryption at rest, but will consider cloud KMS if a bring-your-own-key model is available.
- Redaction: field-level redaction before storage is required; we’d also like an option to redact in-transit at the proxy level if that’s easier for rollout.

Attached is our security_questionnaire.xlsx — this has several specific asks on retention, key rotation, personnel access, and logging export formats. Please review and let us know which items you can close vs need R&D.

Regarding the technical deep-dive: Tue 2026-02-24 10am PT works for us. Please send a calendar invite with call-in details and which internal folks will join.

Also: can you provide a ballpark price for a 6-month pilot supporting ~200 reqs/min sustained, and a 99th pct latency SLA target? We need that to move the pilot through procurement.

Thanks,
Taylor
Taylor Morgan
Director of Product Security, Acme Health
taylor.morgan@acmehealth.com | +1 (650) 555-0110

Attachment: security_questionnaire.xlsx

- KMS: Confirm support for BYOK/HSM options and what timeline is required for implementation (owner: infra team, I’ll open an internal ticket).
- Pilot pricing: I’ll assemble a ballpark for 6 months at 200 reqs/min sustained, include optional add-on for BYOK, and share by EOD tomorrow.

Diego — for the calendar invite please include RSE (will loop in via slack). Also, I started a HubSpot deal RDW-ACME-0067 and attached Taylor’s questionnaire to the record.

Thanks — keeping momentum is important here.

— Aditya
